title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 292bis–293 of the sequel to La Longue Marche): Grothendieck compares the fundamental group of a surface X with a finite group action G to the orbifold fundamental group of the quotient. In his notation, pi_1(X,G) is the extension of G by pi_1(X), and it is identified, by isomorphism (1), with pi_1(Y, d), the orbifold fundamental group of Y = X/G with ramification indices d.

The local comparison, diagram (12). Take X = X^ minus S, a in S, and b = f(a). Let k_a : T_a -> pi_1(X) -> pi_1(X,G) be the outer homomorphism from the local (inertia) group at the puncture a. Then
  k_a = k_b o (d_a . id) o can,
where can : T_a -> T_b is the canonical isomorphism (11) and d_a is the ramification index at a. In words: a small loop around a in X maps to the d_a-th power of the small loop around b in the quotient orbifold.

The application. Take:
- X = U_{0,3}^an = P^1 minus {0, 1, infinity};
- G = S_3, the anharmonic group;
- X^ = Y^ = P^1.
The quotient map is f(z) = (27/4) z^2 (z-1)^2 / (z^2 - z + 1)^3. This is exactly 1728/j(lambda), the inverse of the normalized Klein invariant J. Its fibres are:
- 0, 1, infinity -> 0, each with index 2;
- 2, -1, 1/2 -> 1, each with index 2;
- the primitive sixth roots -j, -j^2 -> infinity, each with index 3.

So Y = P^1 minus {0} is an orbifold with a cusp at 0, a Z/2-point at 1 and a Z/3-point at infinity. Its orbifold group is
  Pi'_{0,3} = < l'_0, l'_1, l'_inf | l'_inf l'_1 l'_0 = 1, l'_1^2 = l'_inf^3 = 1 > = Z/2 * Z/3 = PSL(2,Z).
Grothendieck calls this the oriented triangulated cartographic group C^{+'}_{1,1}, '~ SL(2,Z)'' (prime = mod center).

Isomorphism (15) identifies S^+_{0,3} = pi_1(U_{0,3}, S_3) with this group. This is the classical fact PSL(2,Z)/Gamma(2)-bar = S_3, with Gamma(2)-bar free of rank 2 = pi_1(P^1 minus 3 points).

Table (16), up to conjugacy, gives the images of distinguished elements of S^+_{0,3}:
- The 'half-loops' eps_0, eps_1, eps_inf at the cusps, with eps_i^2 = l_i the loop around i in X, go to l'_0. This is the case d_a = 2 of (12): each cusp has stabilizer Z/2, e.g. z -> z/(z-1) fixes 0 and 2.
- The involutions sigma_0, sigma_1, sigma_inf of S_3 (each fixes one of 0, 1, inf and one of 2, 1/2, -1) go to l'_1.
- The order-3 rotation rho about -j goes to l'_inf. He is unsure whether it is rho or rho^{-1}.

The next page uses this to derive a presentation rho sigma'_0 eps'_0 = 1, rho^3 = sigma'_0^2 = 1 of S^+_{0,3}. It then extends to the non-oriented group S_{0,3} -> GL(2,Z)-type cartographic group via reflections tau, i.e. the extended (2,3,infinity) triangle group.
errors: No mathematical errors found. f is correctly normalized: f(-1)=1, f(-j)=infinity, double zeros at 0, 1, infinity.
The labels 'Pi'_{0,3} = C^{+'}_{1,1} ~ SL(2,Z)'' only make sense if the prime denotes the quotient by the center ±1, since the group defined by (14) is PSL(2,Z).
Grothendieck himself flags an orientation ambiguity: whether rho or rho^{-1} corresponds to l'_inf. This is unresolved on the page.

ideas.what: Compatibility of the inertia maps under a ramified Galois quotient: the local loop at a maps to the d_a-th power of the local loop at b.
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold fundamental group / ramified covering, local inertia comparison
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Riemann–Hurwitz theory; orbifold groups: Thurston, Fox for branched coverings)
ideas.where_published: Similar formalism in SGA1 (tame ramification) but not this exact diagram

ideas.what: The S_3-quotient of P^1 minus {0,1,inf} via f = 1728/j(lambda), with the orbifold quotient having a cusp, an order-2 point and an order-3 point.
ideas.modern_name: Lambda-to-j map; M_{0,4}/S_3 versus M_{1,1}; anharmonic group
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (discussion of M_{0,4}, M_{1,1}, the Teichmüller tower), La Longue Marche

ideas.what: Identification of pi_1(U_{0,3}, S_3) with PSL(2,Z) = Z/2*Z/3, called the oriented triangulated cartographic group, with explicit generators eps_i (square roots of cusp loops), sigma_i (involutions) and rho (order 3).
ideas.modern_name: PSL(2,Z)/Gamma(2) = S_3; cartographic groups / dessins d'enfants; (2,3,infinity) triangle group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical for the group theory; cartographic groups to Grothendieck (Esquisse), developed by Malgoire–Voisin, Jones–Singerman
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §3 (cartographic groups C_2, C_2^+, triangulated case ~ PSL(2,Z)), in general form

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but classical computation: the lambda/j map, PSL(2,Z) as the S_3-orbifold group of the thrice-punctured sphere, and the cartographic-group interpretation already sketched in Esquisse. It is notationally interesting as part of the 'équation des lacets' programme, but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The '2 can' on the upper-left vertical arrow and the '2' on the right vertical arrow are isomorphism signs (≀): '≀ can' (the canonical isomorphism (11)) and '≀'.
'd_g · id' should read 'd_a · id' (the ramification index at a); the bottom right is pi_1(Y, d) with d underlined.
In (16), '(tels que eps_i^2 = sigma_i)' should read '(tels que eps_i^2 = l_i)', the loops around the punctures in X. This is consistent with d_a = 2 in (12).
Under the formula, the fibre over infinity is {-j, -j^2}, the roots of z^2 - z + 1.
